clue.text: Employed by shoe-makers, they're not drunk

definitions.meaning: layers of leather built up to make a shoe's heel, used by cobblers
the dregs of liquor left at the bottom of a glass after drinking

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the leather lifts a cobbler builds a heel from and the last drops left undrunk in a glass.

clue.text: I manage to go mad about nothing but myself with this

definitions.text: I manage to go mad about nothing but myself with this

indicators.note: 'about' means the scrambled letters surround what follows
going mad suggests the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to thinking of nothing but themselves, going mad as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go mad' scrambles I MANAGE into EGMANIA, and 'about' wraps that around O. The whole clue also describes the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessive preoccupation with one's own self and importance is a form of extreme self-centredness.

clue.text: Thirty score in Tennysonian numbers

parts.note: thirty twenties make six hundred, the riders of Tennyson's famous charge, 'numbers' meaning verse

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so thirty score is six hundred: 'Into the valley of Death rode the six hundred' in Tennyson's poem on the Balaclava cavalry charge. 'Numbers' is an old word for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavalry unit of six hundred whose doomed charge at Balaclava Tennyson made famous.

clue.text: A number seen on mural painting out of doors

parts.note: L, the Roman numeral for fifty, is a number
a fresco is a picture painted on wet plaster on a wall

explanation.surface: A figure is visible on a wall painting outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian borrowing means in the open air, as for an outdoor meal.

clue.text: Thus the drunken breed is cured

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy animal breed is somehow cured of its drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' is the definition in the sense of cured of drunkenness, made sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brought back from drunkenness or folly has been made serious and clear-headed, cured of it.

clue.text: Story about a vessel, the Dog-star

indicators.note: 'about' says the fib goes round the words that follow

parts.note: a story can mean a lie, a fib
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A tale about a ship bearing the name of the star Sirius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Dog-star' looks like Sirius but means a film star who is a dog: the collie of the Hollywood films.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie heroine of a long series of films and TV shows is a famous canine celebrity.

clue.text: We hear Nicholas Nye's calling from the hillside

indicators.note: 'We hear' signals a word that is pronounced the same as another

parts.note: Nicholas Nye is the donkey in Walter de la Mare's poem, and a donkey's cry is a bray

explanation.surface: A donkey's cry carries down from the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAE is a Scots word for a hillside or slope.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means a slope or the bank of a hill.

clue.text: Stock controller uses pointed stick going round the river

indicators.note: 'going round' means the stick surrounds the letters that follow

parts.note: a goad is a pointed stick for driving cattle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A herdsman uses a sharp stick to drive animals around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is livestock, here goats, not shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends a flock of goats controls livestock.

clue.text: Composition for a choir or a few instrumentalists? Nothing in it

indicators.note: 'in it' tells us the zero goes inside the group of players just named

parts.note: a trio is a small group of three players, so 'a few instrumentalists' is A TRIO
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a piece is for a choir or a small ensemble, with nothing in it either way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites us to choose between two performing forces; the answer is the choral work itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended sacred work for voices and orchestra, like Handel's Messiah, is a large choral composition.

clue.text: Little consideration for Solomon's work

definitions.meaning: bought 'for a ...' means for very little payment
the ... of Solomon is a book of the Bible ascribed to him

explanation.definitionFit: Something got for a trifling price goes 'for a song', and the biblical Song of Songs is attributed to Solomon.

clue.text: Where many a doctor orders the early rest

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes an early night for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: HARLEY STREET is the London street famous for private medical consultants. 'orders' looks like a doctor's instruction but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is lined with private medical practices and consulting rooms.

clue.text: Cart twice tangled with line is hard to control

indicators.note: tangled letters are knotted up, so they are rearranged
'twice' tells us to take the word cart two times

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A line twisted twice round a cart makes it difficult to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles CART, and 'tangled' mixes CARTCART and LINE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly resisting authority or guidance, like a mule refusing to move.

clue.text: A point is made by one with a jackal's head

parts.note: a nub is the central point of a matter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone making a point about a figure with a jackal's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god of the dead and embalming is shown with the head of a jackal.

clue.text: Perform school task — its object physical training?

definitions.meaning: to carry out or use, as in using one's rights
a piece of work set for pupils to practise a skill
bodily activity done to keep fit, the aim of PT lessons

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers putting a power into use, a set piece of homework, and physical activity for fitness.

clue.text: Caretaker from year's beginning to year's end

definitions.text: Caretaker from year's beginning to year's end

parts.words: Caretaker from year's beginning to year's end
parts.note: alludes to Janus, two-faced Roman god of doorways, after whom January is named; a doorkeeper takes his name from the same Latin root

explanation.walkthrough: Janus looks back to the old year and forward to the new, and a doorkeeper is named from the Latin janua, door.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker of a building was originally a doorkeeper, from Latin janua, door.

clue.text: A prophet's tale of woe

parts.note: the prophet Jeremiah lamented the fall of Jerusalem, and his name gives a word for a doleful complaint

explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Lamentations is traditionally ascribed to Jeremiah, hence a long mournful complaint takes his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lamenting complaint, named after the Hebrew prophet Jeremiah.

clue.text: Like the latest from Mrs Partlet, or from mice and men?

definitions.text: Like the latest from Mrs Partlet, or from mice and men?

parts.words: Like the latest from Mrs Partlet, or from mice and men?
parts.note: Partlet is the hen in Chaucer, so her latest is a fresh egg; Burns's 'best-laid schemes o' mice an' men' gives the second, newest plans

explanation.walkthrough: Dame Partlet is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale; the second half plays on the 'best-laid schemes of mice and men' from Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs just produced by a hen are described as fresh in this way.

clue.text: Made up to insane Baltic statesman

indicators.note: something made up is constructed afresh, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A politician from the Baltic sucks up to someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up to' reads as flattered but 'Made up' is the anagram signal for TO INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman from Estonia, on the Baltic Sea, is a national of that country.

clue.text: Under like pressure one society consumes Italian port

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the society abbreviation surrounds the port

parts.note: Bari is a port on Italy's Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: A single club, under pressure, eats up an Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' means equal, not enjoy: isobars join points of equal pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of equal atmospheric pressure are joined on a weather map by lines of this kind.

clue.text: He doesn't believe in replacement of field

indicators.note: replacement means putting back in new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic refuses to accept that a field can be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement of' rearranges IN and FIELD together.
explanation.definitionFit: A person without religious faith, an unbeliever.

clue.text: Bank owner, dissolute fellow, an old heretic

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a rake or dissolute man
an Arian followed Arius, whose views on the Trinity were condemned in the fourth century

explanation.surface: A list of three disreputable characters: a banker, a rake and a heretic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a riverbank, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A riparian owner holds land along the bank of a river or stream.

clue.text: Harness for trek to see Tyrolean flower outside health resort

indicators.note: 'outside' says the river surrounds the resort

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Inn flows through the Tyrol
a spa is a resort with healing waters

explanation.surface: Tourists in the Tyrol go to admire an alpine bloom near a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, not a bloom. INSPAN is South African for yoking oxen to a wagon for a trek.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa, to yoke draught animals to a wagon before setting out on a journey.

clue.text: Minnows overshadowed by this mollusc?

parts.note: Shakespeare's 'a ... of the minnows' makes the sea god a big fish among small fry, and a large sea snail shares his name

explanation.walkthrough: In Coriolanus, Coriolanus is called a 'Triton of the minnows', one who towers over lesser folk; the same name belongs to a sea snail with a trumpet-like shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea snail with a spiral shell, once blown as a horn, carries the sea god's name.

clue.text: The Spider — or Roundabout (if the swings are unprofitable)

definitions.meaning: a small spider thought to bring wealth to whoever it lands on
from the saying that what you lose on the swings you gain on the roundabouts, so the roundabout is the profitable ride

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a tiny lucky spider and to any venture that brings in plenty of cash, like the profitable fairground ride.

clue.text: Jack said to upset Welsh John here in church

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name reads from the bottom

parts.note: Evan is the Welsh form of John

explanation.surface: A card is played to annoy a Welshman in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wordplays: 'Jack said' also gives it, as Jack is the knave in cards and KNAVE is pronounced the same; 'to upset' turns EVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The central body of a church, where the congregation sits.

clue.text: You may rest here, if it belongs to God

definitions.text: You may rest here, if it belongs to God

parts.words: You may rest here, if it belongs to God
parts.note: 'God's' plot of land is an old name for a churchyard, where the dead rest

explanation.walkthrough: God's acre is an old phrase for a churchyard or burial ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area; with God as owner it is the churchyard, a burial ground.

clue.text: Voice that is lacking in an appointment of a lawyer

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the arrangement to meet

parts.note: a date is an appointment, so 'an appointment' is A DATE

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letters for 'that is' are removed

parts.note: taken as the word itself before letters are removed
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)

explanation.surface: A voice is missing from a meeting arranged with a solicitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' looks like the definition, but the lawyer is the answer; 'lacking' takes IE out of VOICE to leave VOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who pleads cases in court, especially in Scotland, is a kind of barrister.

clue.text: Old gunner's match-holder' — fifty available for sale

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
goods held ready in a shop are in stock

explanation.surface: An antique dealer offers a gunner's match-holder, priced at fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked staff once used by artillerymen to hold the lit slow match for firing a cannon.
